p: Which of the following layers of the medallion architecture is most commonly used by data analysts?

o.a: None of these layers are used by data analysts
o.b: Gold
o.c: All of these layers are used equally by data analysts
o.d: Silver
o.e: Bronze

e: The correct answer is Gold because it represents the refined, aggregated, and business-ready data designed for consumption by data analysts. Data analysts use the Gold layer most often because it provides curated datasets designed for reporting, dashboards, and ad-hoc analysis.

p:
A data analyst has recently joined a new team that uses Databricks SQL, but the analyst has never used Databricks before. The analyst wants to know where in Databricks SQL they can write and execute SQL queries.

On which of the following pages can the analyst write and execute SQL queries?

o.a: Data page
o.b: Dashboards page
o.c: Queries page
o.d: Alerts page
o.e: SQL Editor page

e: The SQL Editor is specifically designed for SQL development. It provides features such as syntax highlighting, auto-completion, query history, and result visualization. Data analysts use this editor to write their queries.

p: Which of the following describes how Databricks SQL should be used in relation to other business intelligence (BI) tools like Tableau, Power BI, and Looker?

o.a: As an exact substitute with the same level of functionality
o.b: As a substitute with less functionality
o.c: As a complete replacement with additional functionality
o.d: As a complementary tool for professional-grade presentations
o.e: As a complementary tool for quick in-platform BI work

e: Databricks SQL complements dedicated BI tools by providing a convenient and efficient means for in-platform data exploration and prototyping, while specialized BI tools are used for advanced analysis and presentation.

p: Which of the following approaches can be used to connect Databricks to Fivetran for data ingestion?

o.a: Use Workflows to establish a SQL warehouse for Fivetran to interact with
o.b: Use Delta Live Tables to establish a cluster for Fivetran to interact with
o.c: Use Partner Connect's automated workflow to establish a cluster for Fivetran to interact with
o.d: Use Partner Connect's automated workflow to establish a SQL warehouse (formerly known as a SQL endpoint) for Fivetran to interact with
o.e: Use Workflows to establish a cluster for Fivetran to interact with

e: Partner Connect streamlines the setup process by automating the creation of the necessary SQL warehouse and configuring the connection details between Fivetran and Databricks.

p:
Data professionals with varying titles use the Databricks SQL service as the primary touchpoint with the Databricks Lakehouse Platform. However, some users will use other services like Databricks Machine Learning or Databricks Data Science and Engineering.

Which of the following roles uses Databric

o.a: Business analyst
o.b: SQL analyst
o.c: Data engineer
o.d: Business intelligence analyst
o.e: Data analyst

e: Data Engineers primarily use Databricks Data Science & Engineering for Spark-based data processing. Databricks SQL functions as a secondary tool for data engineers, assisting in tasks like data validation or troubleshooting.

p:
A data analyst has set up a SQL query to run every four hours on a SQL endpoint, but the SQL endpoint is taking too long to start up with each run.

Which of the following changes can the data analyst make to reduce the start-up time for the endpoint while managing costs?

o.a: Reduce the SQL endpoint cluster size
o.b: Increase the SQL endpoint cluster size
o.c: Turn off the Auto stop feature
o.d: Increase the minimum scaling value
o.e: Use a Serverless SQL endpoint

e: Serverless SQL endpoints eliminate the warm-up period associated with traditional SQL endpoints because they are managed by Databricks, offering immediate compute availability.

p: A data engineering team has created a Structured Streaming pipeline that processes data in micro-batches and populates gold-level tables every minute. A data analyst has created a dashboard based on this data. Stakeholders want the dashboard updated within one minute or less of new data becoming ava

o.a: The required compute resources could be costly
o.b: The gold-level tables are not appropriately clean for business reporting
o.c: The streaming data is not an appropriate data source for a dashboard
o.d: The streaming cluster is not fault tolerant
o.e: The dashboard cannot be refreshed that quickly

e: Continuously querying the gold-level tables every minute to update the dashboard puts a significant load on compute resources. The analyst should caution that this level of frequency might lead to substantial infrastructure costs.

p: Which of the following approaches can be used to ingest data directly from cloud-based object storage?

o.a: Create an external table while specifying the DBFS storage path to FROM
o.b: Create an external table while specifying the DBFS storage path to PATH
o.c: It is not possible to directly ingest data from cloud-based object storage
o.d: Create an external table while specifying the object storage path to FROM
o.e: Create an external table while specifying the object storage path to LOCATION

e: The LOCATION clause in the CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement specifies the path to the data within the object storage. This is the standard method for directly ingesting data.

p:
A data analyst wants to create a dashboard with three main sections: Development, Testing, and Production, and wants to clearly designate the sections using text.

Which of the following tools can the data analyst use to designate these sections using text?

o.a: Separate endpoints for each section
o.b: Separate queries for each section
o.c: Markdown-based text boxes
o.d: Direct text written into the dashboard in editing mode
o.e: Separate color palettes for each section

e: Markdown-based text boxes are the most suitable tool. Databricks dashboards support Markdown, allowing analysts to add formatted text and headings directly within the dashboard interface.

p:
A data analyst needs to use the Databricks Lakehouse Platform to quickly create SQL queries and data visualizations. The solution must support serverless compute and visualizations within a dashboard.

Which service meets all these requirements?

o.a: Delta Lake
o.b: Databricks Notebooks
o.c: Tableau
o.d: Databricks Machine Learning
o.e: Databricks SQL

e: Databricks SQL is designed explicitly for SQL queries, supports serverless compute (Serverless SQL Warehouses), and integrates data visualization capabilities within dashboards.

p: A data analyst is attempting to drop a table my_table...

o.a: The table's data was larger than 10 GB
o.b: The table did not have a location
o.c: The table was external
o.d: The table's data was smaller than 10 GB
o.e: The table was managed

e: When you DROP TABLE for an external table, Databricks only removes the metadata from the metastore. The underlying data files in the external storage location remain untouched.

p: After running `DESCRIBE EXTENDED accounts.customers;`, the Type is listed as `EXTERNAL`...

o.a: Running SELECT * FROM delta.`dbfs:/...` results in an error.
o.b: Running SELECT * FROM accounts.customers will return all rows.
o.c: All files with the customers extension are deleted.
o.d: The table is removed from the metastore, and data files are deleted.
o.e: The table is removed from the metastore, but the underlying data files are untouched.

e: Since this is an external (unmanaged) table, dropping the table only deletes the metadata. The data itself is untouched.

p: Which of the following should data analysts consider when working with personally identifiable information (PII) data?

o.a: Organization-specific best practices for PII data
o.b: Legal requirements for the area in which the data was collected
o.c: None of these considerations
o.d: Legal requirements for the area in which the analysis is being performed
o.e: All of these considerations

e: Responsible data analysis involving PII demands a comprehensive approach that encompasses organizational policies, data origin jurisdiction laws, and the jurisdiction where the analysis is performed.

p: Delta Lake stores table data as a series of data files. Which of the following is stored alongside data files when using Delta Lake?

o.a: None of these
o.b: Table metadata, data summary visualizations, and owner account information
o.c: Table metadata
o.d: Data summary visualizations
o.e: Owner account information

e: Delta Lake meticulously manages metadata (transaction logs, schema info, statistics) alongside data files to provide transactional guarantees and versioning.

p: Which of the following is an advantage of using a Delta Lake-based data lakehouse over common data lake solutions?

o.a: ACID transactions
o.b: Flexible schemas
o.c: Data deletion
o.d: Scalable storage
o.e: Open-source formats

e: Traditional data lakes often lack ACID guarantees. Delta Lake addresses this by providing ACID transactions on top of the data lake, ensuring atomic and consistent updates.

p: Which of the following benefits of using Databricks SQL is provided by Data Explorer?

o.a: It can be used to run UPDATE queries.
o.b: It can be used to view metadata and data, as well as view/change permissions.
o.c: It can be used to produce dashboards.
o.d: It can be used to make visualizations.
o.e: It can be used to connect to third party BI tools.

e: Data Explorer is designed for discovery and governance. It allows users to view metadata (schema, types), preview data, and manage permissions on data assets.

p: The stakeholders.customers table has 15 columns and 3,000 rows...

o.a: The view remains available and SELECT * FROM stakeholders.eur_customers will execute correctly.
o.b: The view has been dropped.
o.c: The view is not available in the metastore, but the underlying data can be accessed with SELECT * FROM delta.`stakeholders.eur_customers`.
o.d: The view remains available but attempting to SELECT from it results in an empty result set because data in views are automatically deleted after logging out.
o.e: The view has been converted into a table.

e: TEMPORARY views are visible only to the session that created them and are dropped automatically when the session ends (e.g., user logs out).

p:
A data analyst created and is the owner of the managed table my_ table. They now want to change ownership of the table to a single other user using Data Explorer.
Which of the following approaches can the analyst use to complete the task?

o.a: Edit the Owner field in the table page by removing their own account
o.b: Edit the Owner field in the table page by selecting All Users
o.c: Edit the Owner field in the table page by selecting the new owner's account
o.d: Edit the Owner field in the table page by selecting the Admins group
o.e: Edit the Owner field in the table page by removing all access

e: The correct method is to explicitly assign the new owner's account in the Owner field. This ensures a clear transfer of responsibility and privileges.

p: A data analyst has a managed table `table_name` in database `database_name`. They would now like to remove the table from the database and all of the data files associated with the table. The rest of the tables in the database must continue to exist.\n\nWhich of the following commands can the analys

o.a: DROP DATABASE database_name;
o.b: DROP TABLE database_name.table_name;
o.c: DELETE TABLE database_name.table_name;
o.d: DELETE TABLE table_name FROM database_name;
o.e: DROP TABLE table_name FROM database_name;

e: When used with a managed table, `DROP TABLE` removes both the table's metadata from the metastore and the underlying data files. `database_name.table_name` specifies the target table correctly.

p:
A data analyst runs the following command:

```sql
SELECT age, country
FROM my_table
WHERE age >= 75 AND country = 'canada';
```

Which of the following tables represents the output of the above command?

o.a:
| age | country |
|---|---|
| 80 | canada |
| NULL | canada |
| 90 | NULL |
o.b:
| age | country |
|---|---|
| 80 | NULL |
| 75 | NULL |
| 90 | NULL |
o.c:
| id | age | country |
|---|---|---|
| 900 | 80 | canada |
| 901 | 75 | canada |
| 902 | 90 | canada |
o.d:
| age | country |
|---|---|
| 80 | canada |
| 14 | canada |
| 90 | canada |
o.e:
| age | country |
|---|---|
| 80 | canada |
| 75 | canada |
| 90 | canada |

e: The query filters for `age >= 75` AND `country = 'canada'`. Option E is the only table where all rows satisfy both conditions (Age is 75, 80, 90 and Country is 'canada') and only the selected columns are shown.

p:
A data analyst runs the following command:

```sql
INSERT INTO stakeholders.suppliers TABLE stakeholders.new_suppliers;
```

What is the result of running this command?

o.a: The suppliers table now contains both the data it had before and the data from new_suppliers, and duplicates are deleted.
o.b: The command fails because it is written incorrectly.
o.c: The suppliers table now contains both the data it had before and the data from new_suppliers, including any duplicate data.
o.d: The suppliers table now contains the data from the new_suppliers table, and new_suppliers contains data from suppliers.
o.e: The suppliers table now contains only the data from the new_suppliers table.

e: The `INSERT INTO ... TABLE` command appends data from the source table to the target table. It does not automatically remove duplicate rows; if duplicates exist in the source, they are added.

p: A data engineer is working with a nested array column products...

o.a: array distinct(products)
o.b: explode(products)
o.c: reduce(products)
o.d: array(products)
o.e: flatten(products)

e: `explode(products)` takes an array column and creates a new row for each element in the array, duplicating the other columns for each new row.

p:
A data analysis team is working with the table_bronze SQL table as a source for one of its most complex projects. A stakeholder of the project notices that some of the downstream data is duplicative. The analysis team identifies table_bronze as the source of the duplication.
Which of the following q
e: `SELECT DISTINCT *` is the standard SQL clause to retrieve only unique rows. Combining this with `CREATE TABLE ... AS` creates a new table with the deduplicated data.

p: A business analyst has been asked to create a data entity/object called sales_by_employee. It should always stay up-to-date when new data are added to the sales table. The new entity should have the columns sales_person, which will be the name of the employee from the employees table, and sales, whi
e: A View (`CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`) is a virtual table defined by a query. It does not store data itself but runs the query every time it is accessed, ensuring the data is always up-to-date.

p: A data analyst has been asked to use the below table sales_table...
e: `PERCENT_RANK()` calculates the relative rank (0 to 1). `PARTITION BY region` ensures the calculation is done independently for each region. `ORDER BY sales DESC` ranks higher sales first (0) and lower sales last (1).

p: In which of the following situations should a data analyst use higher-order functions?

o.a: When custom logic needs to be applied to simple, unnested data
o.b: When custom logic needs to be converted to Python-native code
o.c: When custom logic needs to be applied at scale to array data objects
o.d: When built-in functions are taking too long to perform tasks
o.e: When built-in functions need to run through the Catalyst Optimizer

e: Higher-order functions in Spark SQL (like `transform`, `filter` on arrays) are designed to apply custom logic efficiently to elements within complex data types like arrays and maps without exploding them.

p: Consider two statements using LEFT SEMI JOIN and LEFT ANTI JOIN...

o.a: The first statement will return all data from the customers table and matching data from the orders table. The second statement will return all data from the orders table and matching data from the cu
o.b: When the first statement is run, only rows from the customers table that have at least one match with the orders table on customer_id will be returned. When the second statement is run, only those row
o.c: There is no difference between the result sets for both statements.
o.d: Both statements will fail because Databricks SQL does not support those join types.
o.e: When the first statement is run, all rows from the customers table will be returned and only the customer_id from the orders table will be returned. When the second statement is run, only those rows i

e: `LEFT SEMI JOIN` returns rows from the left table that have a match in the right. `LEFT ANTI JOIN` returns rows from the left table that do NOT have a match in the right.

p: A data analyst has created a UDF... Which code block applies this function?
e: To apply a UDF, you call it like a standard function, passing the column names as arguments: `price(col1, col2)`.

p: A data analyst has written a query to count customers per region...

o.a: The query is using count(*), which will count all the customers in the customers table, no matter the region.
o.b: The query is missing a GROUP BY region clause.
o.c: The query is using ORDER BY, which is not allowed in an aggregation.
o.d: There are no mistakes in the query.
o.e: The query is selecting region, but region should only occur in the ORDER BY clause.

e: When using an aggregate function like `COUNT` with a non-aggregated column like `region`, a `GROUP BY` clause is required to define the groups.

p: A data analyst is processing a complex aggregation... Which query produced the result?
e: `WITH CUBE` generates subtotals for all possible combinations of the grouping columns (totals for group_1, totals for group_2, and the grand total).

p: Which of the following is a benefit of Databricks SQL using ANSI SQL as its standard SQL dialect?

o.a: It has increased customization capabilities
o.b: It is easy to migrate existing SQL queries to Databricks SQL
o.c: It allows for the use of Photon's computation optimizations
o.d: It is more performant than other SQL dialects
o.e: It is more compatible with Spark's interpreters

e: ANSI SQL compliance ensures broad compatibility, making it significantly easier to migrate existing queries and workloads from other systems to Databricks.

p: How can a data analyst determine if query results were pulled from the cache?

o.a: Go to the Query History tab and click on the text of the query. The slideout shows if the results came from the cache.
o.b: Go to the Alerts tab and check the Cache Status alert.
o.c: Go to the Queries tab and click on Cache Status. The status will be green if the results from the last run came from the cache.
o.d: Go to the SQL Warehouse (formerly SQL Endpoints) tab and click on Cache. The Cache file will show the contents of the cache.
o.e: Go to the Data tab and click Last Query. The details of the query will show if the results came from the cache.

e: Query History provides execution details for each query. Clicking on a specific query reveals a slideout with metadata, including whether the result was fetched from the cache.

p: Which of the following statements about a refresh schedule is **incorrect**?

o.a: A query can be refreshed anywhere from 1 minute to 2 weeks.
o.b: Refresh schedules can be configured in the Query Editor.
o.c: A query being refreshed on a schedule does not use a SQL Warehouse.
o.d: A refresh schedule is not the same as an alert.
o.e: You must have workspace administrator privileges to configure a refresh schedule.

e: You do NOT need to be an admin to schedule a refresh. Typically, the query owner or users with 'Can Manage' permissions on the query can configure schedules.

p:
A data analyst creates a Databricks SQL Query where the result set has the following schema: region STRING number_of_customer INT
When the analyst clicks on the "Add visualization" button on the SQL Editor page, which of the following types of visualizations will be selected by default?

o.a: Violin Chart
o.b: Line Chart
o.c: Bar Chart
o.d: Histogram
o.e: There is no default. The user must choose a visualization type.

e: Databricks heuristics often default to a Line Chart when analyzing a quantitative value (`number_of_customer`) against a qualitative or categorical value (`region`), although a Bar Chart might also be appropriate.

p:
A data analyst has created a Query in Databricks SQL, and now they want to create two data visualizations from that Query and add both of those data visualizations to the same Databricks SQL Dashboard.
Which of the following steps will they need to take when creating and adding both data visualizati

o.a: They will need to alter the Query to return two separate sets of results.
o.b: They will need to add two separate visualizations to the dashboard based on the same Query.
o.c: They will need to create two separate dashboards.
o.d: They will need to decide on a single data visualization to add to the dashboard.
o.e: They will need to copy the Query and create one data visualization per query.

e: You can create multiple visualization widgets from a single query execution and add them individually to a dashboard without duplicating the underlying query.

p:
A data analyst has been asked to provide a list of options on how to share a dashboard with a client. It is a security requirement that the client does not gain access to any other information, resources, or artifacts in the database.
Which of the following approaches cannot be used to share the das

o.a: Download the Dashboard as a PDF and share it with the client.
o.b: Set a refresh schedule for the dashboard and enter the client's email address in the "Subscribers" box.
o.c: Take a screenshot of the dashboard and share it with the client.
o.d: Generate a Personal Access Token that is good for 1 day and share it with the client.
o.e: Download a PNG file of the visualizations in the dashboard and share them with the client.

e: Sharing a Personal Access Token (PAT) gives the client authenticated access to the API and potential resources acting as that user, violating the security requirement.

p: A data analyst has been asked to produce a visualization that shows the flow of users through a website. Which of the following is used for visualizing this type of flow?

o.a: Heatmap
o.b: Choropleth
o.c: Word Cloud
o.d: Pivot Table
o.e: Sankey

e: A Sankey diagram is specifically designed to visualize flows, transfers, and movements between different states or stages.

p:
An analyst writes a query that contains a query parameter. They then add an area chart visualization to the query. While adding the area chart visualization to a dashboard, the analyst chooses "Dashboard Parameter" for the query parameter associated with the area chart.

Which of the following state

o.a: The area chart will use whatever is selected in the Dashboard Parameter while all or the other visualizations will remain changed regardless of their parameter use.
o.b: The area chart will use whatever is selected in the Dashboard Parameter along with all of the other visualizations in the dashboard that use the same parameter.
o.c: The area chart will use whatever value is chosen on the dashboard at the time the area chart is added to the dashboard.
o.d: The area chart will use whatever value is input by the analyst when the visualization is added to the dashboard. The parameter cannot be changed by the user afterwards.
o.e: The area chart will convert to a Dashboard Parameter.

e: When linked to a Dashboard Parameter, the visualization shares the control with other widgets using the same parameter, allowing a single selection to update multiple charts simultaneously.

p:
A data analyst has been asked to configure an alert for a query that returns the income in the `accounts_receivable` table for a date range. The date range is configurable using a Date query parameter. The Alert does not work.

Which of the following describes why the Alert does not work?

o.a: Alerts don't work with queries that access tables.
o.b: Queries that return results based on dates cannot be used with Alerts.
o.c: The wrong query parameter is being used. Alerts only work with Date and Time query parameters.
o.d: Queries that use query parameters cannot be used with Alerts.
o.e: The wrong query parameter is being used. Alerts only work with dropdown list query parameters, not dates.

e: Queries that use query parameters introduce dynamic behavior that cannot be consistently evaluated by the alerting system. Databricks Alerts require a static query.

p: Which of the following statements about adding visual appeal to visualizations in the Visualization Editor is incorrect?

o.a: Visualization scale can be changed.
o.b: Data Labels can be formatted.
o.c: Colors can be changed.
o.d: Borders can be added.
o.e: Tooltips can be formatted.

e: The Visualization Editor does not provide a feature to add borders around the visualization. It focuses on data representation aspects like scale, colors, and labels.

p: A data team has been given a series of projects by a consultant that need to be implemented in the Databricks Lakehouse Platform. Which of the following projects should be completed in Databricks SQL?

o.a: Testing the quality of data as it is imported from a source
o.b: Tracking usage of feature variables for machine learning projects
o.c: Combining two data sources into a single, comprehensive dataset
o.d: Segmenting customers into like groups using a clustering algorithm
o.e: Automating complex notebook-based workflows with multiple tasks

e: Databricks SQL excels at data warehousing tasks such as querying, joining, and aggregating data from different sources to create comprehensive datasets.

p: A data organization has a team of engineers developing data pipelines following the medallion architecture using Delta Live Tables. While the data analysis team working on a project is using gold-layer tables from these pipelines, they need to perform some additional processing of these tables prior

o.a: Data blending
o.b: Last-mile dashboarding
o.c: Data testing
o.d: Last-mile ETL
o.e: Data enhancement

e: This type of light, custom processing performed by analysts on top of the refined gold layer is often referred to as Last-mile ETL.

p: Which of the following statements describes descriptive statistics?

o.a: A branch of statistics that uses summary statistics to quantitatively describe and summarize data.
o.b: A branch of statistics that uses a variety of data analysis techniques to infer properties of an underlying distribution of probability.
o.c: A branch of statistics that uses quantitative variables that must take on a finite or countably infinite set of values.
o.d: A branch of statistics that uses summary statistics to categorically describe and summarize data.
o.e: A branch of statistics that uses quantitative variables that must take on an uncountable set of values.

e: Descriptive statistics focuses on using measures like mean, median, and mode to summarize and present the characteristics of a dataset.

p: In which of the following situations will the mean value and median value of variable be meaningfully different?

o.a: When the variable contains no outliers
o.b: When the variable contains no missing values
o.c: When the variable is of the boolean type
o.d: When the variable is of the categorical type
o.e: When the variable contains a lot of extreme outliers

e: Extreme outliers pull the mean towards them (skewing the distribution), while the median remains resistant, resulting in a significant difference between the two.

p:
A data analyst is working with gold-layer tables to complete an ad-hoc project. A stakeholder has provided the analyst with an additional dataset that can be used to augment the gold-layer tables already in use.

Which of the following terms is used to describe this data augmentation?

o.a: Data testing
o.b: Ad-hoc improvements
o.c: Last-mile dashboarding
o.d: Last-mile ETL
o.e: Data enhancement

e: Data enhancement is the process where data is made richer or more complete by adding new datasets to improve the utility of the original data.

p:
A data analyst needs to query the data in `my_table`. They want to return the values in columns `user_id` and `email_address` where records fit the following filter criteria: `age` is greater than 25 and `country` is Canada. The analyst does not want to return values from any other columns.

Which c
e: This query correctly selects only the `user_id` and `email_address` columns and applies the filter `age > 25` and `country = 'Canada'`.

p: Which example of data projects represents a common analytics application to be completed in Databricks SQL?

o.a: Augmenting gold-layer tables with additional external information
o.b: Automating complex notebook-based workflows with multiple tasks
o.c: Testing the quality of data as it is imported from a source
o.d: Segmenting customers into like groups using a clustering algorithm

e: Working with gold-layer tables (clean, business-ready data) and performing additional joins or enhancements is a typical use case for Databricks SQL.

p: What is a benefit of using Databricks SQL for business intelligence (BI) analytics projects instead of using third-party BI tools?

o.a: Computations, data, and analytical tools on the same platform
o.b: Advanced dashboarding capabilities
o.c: Simultaneous multi-user support
o.d: Automated alerting systems

e: It unifies computations, data storage, and analytical tools on the same platform, avoiding the need to move data out of the lakehouse for analysis.

p: A data analyst wants the following output...
e: The query requires a `COUNT(order_id)` and a `GROUP BY customer_name`. (Note: The source marks 'C' as the answer but Option D contains the correct standard SQL syntax with 'AS' and 'GROUP BY'. The provided explanation matches the logic of Option D).

p: What is an advantage of using a Delta Lake-based data lakehouse over classic enterprise data warehouse solutions?

o.a: Open-source formats
o.b: Schema enforcement
o.c: ACID transactions
o.d: Generic optimizations

e: While classic EDWs have ACID, the question in this exam context highlights ACID as a key feature brought by Delta Lake to the Lakehouse architecture.

p:
Query History provides Databricks SQL users with a lot of benefits. A data analyst has been asked to share all of these benefits with their team as part of a training exercise. One of the benefit statements the analyst provided to their team is incorrect.

Which statement about Query History is inco

o.a: It can be used to troubleshoot slow running queries.
o.b: It can be used to view the query plan of queries that have run.
o.c: It can be used to debug queries.
o.d: It can be used to automate query execution on multiple warehouses (formerly endpoints).

e: Query History monitors past executions but does not have functionality to automate or schedule future query executions.

p: A data scientist has asked a data analyst to create histograms for every continuous variable in a data set. What describes a continuous variable?

o.a: A quantitative variable that never stops changing
o.b: A quantitative variable that can take on a finite or countably infinite set of values
o.c: A quantitative variable that can take on an uncountable set of values
o.d: A categorical variable in which the number of categories continues to increase over time

e: A continuous variable can take on any value within a range (uncountable), including fractions and decimals.

p: A data analyst has been asked to use the below table sales_table to rank products within region by the sales. Which query will accomplish this task?
e: To rank strictly *within* regions as requested, `PARTITION BY region` is usually required, while `ORDER BY sales DESC` ranks them by sales.

p: A database was created in Databricks SQL using the following statement...

o.a: dbfs:/accounting/data/accounting.db
o.b: dbfs:/accounting/data
o.c: dbfs:/accounting/data.db
o.d: dbfs:/user/hive/warehouse/accounting.db

e: Unless the location is specified at the *table* level or configured differently, managed databases in the Hive metastore typically default to the warehouse directory `dbfs:/user/hive/warehouse/accounting.db`.

p: A data analyst is processing a complex aggregation on a table with zero null values...
e: `WITH ROLLUP` generates subtotals for the specified columns in a hierarchical manner (e.g., total for group_1, and grand total), which matches the output shown.

p: A managed table and an unmanaged (external) table were both created in Databricks SQL, and data were ingested into each table. Later, both tables were dropped. What is the status of data for each of those tables?

o.a: The data in both tables were deleted.
o.b: The data in the managed table were deleted, and the data in the unmanaged (external) table were left untouched.
o.c: The data in the unmanaged (external) table were deleted and the data in the managed table were left untouched.
o.d: The data in both tables were left untouched.

e: Dropping a managed table deletes both metadata and data. Dropping an external table deletes only the metadata, leaving the underlying data files intact.

p: Which statement about subqueries is correct?

o.a: Subqueries are not available in Databricks SQL.
o.b: Subqueries can be used like other user-defined functions to transform data into different data types.
o.c: Subqueries can retrieve data without requiring the creation of a table or view.
o.d: Subqueries can be used like other built-in functions to transform data into different data types.

e: Subqueries allow you to retrieve and use data dynamically within another query without the need to formally define and create a persistent table or view.

p: Which location can be used to determine the owner of a managed table?

o.a: Review the Owner field in the table page using Catalog Explorer
o.b: Review the Owner field in the database page using Data Explorer
o.c: Review the Owner field in the schema page using Data Explorer
o.d: Review the Owner field in the table page using the SQL Editor

e: Catalog Explorer provides detailed metadata for objects in Unity Catalog, including the Owner field for tables.

p: Which statement about visualizations is true?

o.a: All visualizations must use the same data in order to be included in the same Databricks SQL dashboard.
o.b: Line charts are the preferred visualization type for categorical data.
o.c: Different visualizations can be used to tell different stories about the data.
o.d: There is no difference between the bar chart and a histogram in Databricks SQL.

e: Visualizations are tools for communication; choosing different types (bar, line, scatter) highlights different aspects, trends, or relationships within the same dataset.

p: What describes the variance of a set of values?

o.a: Variance is a measure of how far a single observed value is from a set of values.
o.b: Variance is a measure of how far an observed value is from the variable's maximum or minimum value.
o.c: Variance is a measure of central tendency of a set of values.
o.d: Variance is a measure of how far a set of values is spread out from the set's central value.

e: Variance quantifies the spread or dispersion of a dataset relative to its mean (central value).

p: Which SQL standards does Databricks SQL use as its default SQL dialect?

o.a: Databricks SQL
o.b: Spark SQL
o.c: ANSI
o.d: Delta SQL

e: Databricks SQL uses ANSI SQL as its standard dialect, ensuring broad compatibility with other systems and standard SQL syntax.

p:
A data analyst is working in an organization that utilizes a multi-hop, medallion architecture. They have been tasked with creating a new Gold table from an existing Silver table.

Which query is performing a hop from a Silver table to a Gold table?
e: Moving from Silver (`cleaned_transactions`) to Gold involves aggregation and business logic. Option C aggregates sales by store, which is typical for a Gold-level business report.

p: What is used as a compute resource for Databricks SQL?

o.a: Standard clusters
o.b: Single-node clusters
o.c: SQL warehouses
o.d: Downstream BI tools integrated with Databricks SQL

e: SQL Warehouses are the optimized compute engines dedicated to executing SQL queries in Databricks SQL.

p: A data analyst has opened up the SQL Editor page and written a new SQL statement. The data analyst now wants to save that statement to easily refer back to it later to add it to a dashboard. The results of the SQL statement must be able to be displayed as a counter, table, or a data visualization.

o.a: Save the SQL statement as a Dashboard
o.b: Save the SQL statement within a Notebook
o.c: Save the SQL statement as a Query
o.d: Save the SQL statement in the Query History page

e: Saving as a Query object is the standard way to persist SQL statements in Databricks SQL for reuse and dashboard integration.

p: A data analyst wants to create a Databricks SQL dashboard with multiple data visualizations and multiple counters. What must be completed before adding the data visualizations and counters to the dashboard?

o.a: All data visualizations and counters must be created using Queries.
o.b: A SQL warehouse must be turned on and selected.
o.c: A markdown-based tile must be added to the top of the dashboard.
o.d: The dashboard owner must also be the owner of the queries.

e: Visualizations and counters in a dashboard are built on top of Queries. You must create and save these Queries (and their associated visualizations) first.

p: An analyst has been asked to combine the data in two tables: suppliers and new_suppliers. It's possible that some of the supplier_id values match in both tables, meaning that those particular suppliers have already been added to the suppliers table. If that is the case, the data should be unchanged.
e: `MERGE INTO` allows conditional logic. `WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *` ensures only new records are added, preventing duplicates for existing IDs.

p: What does Partner Connect do when connecting Power BI and Tableau?

o.a: Creates a PAT, downloads/installs ODBC driver, and downloads a configuration file for connection to a SQL Warehouse.
o.b: Creates a PAT and emails it to you.
o.c: Downloads a configuration file only.
o.d: Downloads and installs an ODBC driver only.

e: Partner Connect simplifies the connection process by automating the creation of security tokens (PAT), obtaining drivers, and providing pre-configured connection files.

p: A data analyst is working with a nested array column products... The analyst wants to return the first item...

o.a: products.1
o.b: products.0
o.c: products[0]
o.d: products[1]

e: Databricks SQL (and Spark SQL) uses 0-based indexing for array access with bracket notation. `products[0]` retrieves the first element.

p:
A dashboard contains a bar chart visualization. The bar chart has a Date widget parameter associated with it.

Which statement about the Date widget parameter is true?

o.a: The Date widget parameter provides a start date and an end date that is used by a WHERE clause in the query that provides data to the bar chart.
o.b: The Date widget parameter provides a start date and an end date that sets the x-axis range of the bar chart.
o.c: The Date widget parameter provides a start date and an end date that filters all visualizations in the dashboard.
o.d: The Date widget parameter functions only as a text box that tells the dashboard's users what date range the dashboard is using.

e: Widget parameters pass values (like a date range) into the underlying query's SQL code (typically in a WHERE clause) to filter the data before it is visualized.

p: A data analyst needs to share a Databricks SQL dashboard with stakeholders who do not have Databricks accounts. The stakeholders need to be notified every time the dashboard is refreshed. Which approach minimizes effort?

o.a: By granting the stakeholders' email addresses permissions to the dashboard
o.b: By adding the stakeholders' email addresses to the refresh schedule subscribers list
o.c: By adding the stakeholders' email addresses to the SQL Warehouse subscribers list
o.d: By downloading the dashboard as a PDF and emailing it manually

e: You can add non-account email addresses to a dashboard's scheduled refresh subscription. They will receive an email snapshot of the dashboard automatically.

p: What describes Partner Connect in Databricks?

o.a: It allows for free use of Databricks partner tools through a common API.
o.b: It allows multi-directional connection between Databricks and Databricks partners easier.
o.c: It exposes connection information to third-party tools via Databricks partners.
o.d: It is a feature that runs Databricks partner tools on a Databricks SQL Warehouse.

e: Partner Connect simplifies the integration process, making it easier to establish data connections between Databricks and various partner ecosystems (BI, ingestion, etc.)

p: In which scenario should a data analyst create and use a user-defined function (UDF)?

o.a: When the result of logic needs to be restricted to certain users
o.b: When logic needs to be deployed within a subquery
o.c: When complex logic cannot be implemented with built-in capabilities
o.d: When simple logic needs to be optimized for scaling purposes

e: UDFs are designed to encapsulate custom, often complex logic that isn't available through standard built-in SQL functions, allowing for reusability.

p: A data analyst has produced a visualization. A stakeholder has viewed the visualization and is complaining that the visualization is difficult to interpret. After looking at the visualization, the analyst determines that the scale of the y-axis must be changed. Where are the controls for changing th

o.a: Query Editor -> Y Axis
o.b: Dashboard Editor -> Axes -> Y Axis
o.c: Visualization Editor -> Y Axis
o.d: Settings -> User Settings -> Scaling

e: To change specific chart properties like axis scales, labels, or ranges, you must access the specific configuration within the Visualization Editor.

p: A data analyst has two data sources that are providing similar but complementary information. The analyst wants to combine these sources of data into a single, comprehensive dataset for ongoing use for their team in a variety of different projects. Which terms is used to describe this type of work?

o.a: Last-mile ETL
o.b: Ad-hoc improvements
o.c: Data testing
o.d: Data blending

e: Data blending refers to the process of combining data from multiple sources into a unified dataset to create a more comprehensive view for analysis.

p: A data analyst has been asked to determine which customers have placed an order in the past year and which customers have not placed an order in the past year. This can be determined with one statement by joining the `customers` table (which is unique by customer ID) and the `orders` table. Which ty

o.a: Left Semi Join
o.b: Left Join
o.c: Middle Join
o.d: Left Anti Join

e: A Left Join returns all records from the left table (`customers`) and matched records from the right (`orders`). This allows identifying customers with orders (match) and those without (NULL on the right side) in a single result set.

p: A data analyst has come across a column in a table that contains personally identifiable information (PII). The data analyst should not have access to this type of PII data. How should the data analyst proceed?

o.a: Stop working with the data and delete the table and any existing metadata or data files.
o.b: Stop working with the data and proceed with the project using other data.
o.c: Stop working with the data and notify their supervisor to ensure the data is handled following organizational and legal best practices.
o.d: Drop the column containing PII data and continue with the project without notifying anybody.

e: The correct protocol is to immediately stop accessing the unauthorized data and escalate to a supervisor to ensure compliance with legal and organizational policies.

p: A data engineering team has created a Structured Streaming pipeline that processes data in micro-batches and populates gold-level tables. The microbatches are triggered every 10 minutes. A data analyst has created a dashboard based on this gold-level data. The project stakeholders want to see the re

o.a: A refresh schedule with an always-on SQL Warehouse (formerly known as SQL Endpoint)
o.b: A refresh schedule with an interval of 10 minutes or less
o.c: A refresh schedule with stakeholders included as subscribers
o.d: A refresh schedule with a Structured Streaming cluster

e: To meet the stakeholder requirement of seeing new data within 10 minutes, the dashboard must be scheduled to refresh at an interval matching or exceeding that frequency (10 minutes or less).

p: Where in the Databricks SQL workspace can a data analyst configure a refresh schedule for a query when the query is not attached to a dashboard or alert?

o.a: Data Explorer
o.b: The Visualization Editor
o.c: The Query Editor
o.d: The Dashboard Editor

e: Queries can be scheduled to run independently directly from the Query Editor interface.

p: A stakeholder has provided a data analyst with a lookup dataset in the form of a 50-row CSV file. The data analyst needs to upload this dataset for use as a table in Databricks SQL. Which approach should the data analyst use to quickly upload the file into a table for use in Databricks SQL?

o.a: Create a table by uploading the file using the Create page within Databricks SQL.
o.b: Create a table via a connection between Databricks and the desktop facilitated by Partner Connect.
o.c: Create a table by uploading the file to cloud storage and then importing the data to Databricks.
o.d: Create a table by manually copying and pasting the data values into cloud storage and then importing the data to Databricks.

e: The 'Create' page in Databricks SQL allows for a simple drag-and-drop upload of small CSV files to quickly create a table, which is ideal for a 50-row lookup file.

p: Which open-source project helps to enable the data lakehouse by adding organization, reliability, performance, and data governance to data lake architectures?

o.a: MLflow
o.b: Apache Spark
o.c: Delta Lake
o.d: Databricks SQL

e: Delta Lake is the storage layer that adds ACID transactions, schema enforcement, and reliability to the data lake, enabling the Lakehouse architecture.

p: Which data visualization use cases is best completed using Databricks SQL relative to other visualization tools?

o.a: Presentation-grade visualizations for publication
o.b: Organization-branded visualizations for marketing material
o.c: Custom, interactive visualizations on small data
o.d: Simple, exploratory visualizations on big data

e: Databricks SQL visualizations are optimized for quick, exploratory analysis directly on large datasets residing in the lakehouse, rather than pixel-perfect polished presentations.

p: A data analyst has written and saved a series of queries that reveal trends that need to be monitored by several stakeholders. Which tool should the data analyst use to share the results of all of the queries to be viewed at once?

o.a: A SQL warehouse (formerly known as a SQL endpoint)
o.b: A Query History page
o.c: A dashboard
o.d: A data visualization tab on a Query page

e: Dashboards allow you to combine visualizations from multiple queries into a single view that can be easily shared with stakeholders.

p: A data analyst needs to create an empty managed table `table_name` in database `database_name` with a specific schema. The table needs to be recreated and empty, regardless of whether or not the table already exists. Which command can the analyst use to complete the task?
e: `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` ensures the table is dropped and recreated if it exists. Defining columns in parentheses `(col type, ...)` is the standard syntax for defining the schema.

p: Data professionals with varying responsibilities use the Databricks Lakehouse Platform. Which role in the Databricks Lakehouse Platform use Databricks SQL as their primary service?

o.a: Data scientist
o.b: Data engineer
o.c: Platform architect
o.d: Business analyst

e: Business analysts are the primary audience for Databricks SQL, using it for ad-hoc queries, reporting, and dashboards.

p: A data analyst tries to calculate daily sales but gets multiple rows... Which corrected query produces exactly one row per product per day?
e: Using `GROUP BY product_id, sale_date` with the aggregate function `SUM(sale_amount)` correctly collapses the rows to the desired granularity (one row per product/day).

p:
A data analyst is migrating data lakehouse workloads to Databricks. The analyst manages a large table with thousands of columns and several billion rows. The analyst is concerned about scan performance, query speed, and handling the overhead of processing such a large volume of data.

In which two w

o.a: Photon leverages a columnar, vectorized execution engine for efficient scan and aggregation operations.
o.b: Photon automatically merges small files into a single large file before processing.
o.c: Photon processes data row by row for maximum compatibility with legacy systems.
o.d: Photon automatically parallelizes all queries across multiple clusters without additional configuration.
o.e: Photon uses a caching layer to transcode data into a CPU-efficient format for faster scan performance.

e: Photon improves performance on large datasets using a vectorized C++ execution engine (A) and a specialized caching layer that transcodes data for faster scanning (E).

p: A data analyst is setting up a Genie space in Databricks. Which sequence should the analyst use for defining reasonable sample questions to help guide user interactions and improve Genie's accuracy?

o.a: Click "Configure" > "Context" in the Genie space, use the "SQL Queries" tab to add sample questions and matching SQL, then review and resolve any inconsistencies in the guidance provided.
o.b: Create a dedicated notebook for each sample question, write the corresponding SQL query in the notebook, and link these notebooks to the Genie space using a workspace object reference.
o.c: Navigate to "Configure" > "Settings" and enter the sample questions directly into the "Description" field. Genie automatically parses this text to guide users.
o.d: Upload a spreadsheet with sample questions to the space, manually map each question to a SQL query in a separate document, and periodically update the mappings as new questions arise.

e: The correct workflow for training Genie is to provide sample questions and their corresponding correct SQL directly in the configuration context menu.

p: A data analyst team is building reliable, production-grade data pipelines on Databricks. They require a solution that allows them to define data transformations declaratively, automatically enforce data quality expectations, and handle errors without manual intervention. Which Databricks capability

o.a: Lakeflow Jobs
o.b: Lakeflow Tables
o.c: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
o.d: Lakeflow Connect

e: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (often referring to Delta Live Tables logic) are designed for declarative ETL with built-in quality expectations and automated orchestration.

p: A data analyst is evaluating options to optimize query performance on a large table with frequently changing query filters. The analyst is considering using Liquid Clustering versus traditional Hive-style partitioning. What is the primary advantage of Liquid Clustering over traditional partitioning

o.a: Liquid Clustering allows changing clustering columns without rewriting existing data, while partitioning requires reprocessing and rewriting data to change the partitioning structure.
o.b: Liquid Clustering supports more data types than partitioning, including nested structures and arrays.
o.c: Liquid Clustering provides better compression ratios than partitioned tables, reducing storage costs.
o.d: Liquid Clustering automatically creates backup copies of data files, while partitioning does not.

e: Liquid Clustering offers flexibility to change clustering keys on the fly without the expensive rewrite required by traditional partitioning, adapting to evolving query patterns.

p: A data analyst uses Databricks to create a dashboard that monitors daily sales volumes and store performance. To ensure that area managers always see up-to-date data without having to manually intervene, the data analyst wants to automate the dashboard data refresh. Which process should the data ana

o.a: Export the dashboard as a PDF the night before, so the team can see "recent" data the next day.
o.b: Use the dashboard's built-in scheduling option to set an automatic refresh at regular intervals.
o.c: Set the Dashboard query to 'auto-update' by using a browser extension that reloads the tab at set intervals.
o.d: Ask all users to press the "Refresh" button on the dashboard whenever they want updated data.

e: Databricks dashboards can be scheduled to refresh automatically at specified intervals, ensuring stakeholders always view the most current data without manual effort.

p:
A data analyst is configuring a Genie space to support natural language questions about product sales, including fields like `region_code`, `sku`, and `channel_type`. The analyst notices that Genie often generates ambiguous or incorrect queries due to unclear column meanings.

Which two actions will

o.a: Provide sample values for ambiguous columns to help Genie infer the data's meaning and usage.
o.b: Write domain-specific instructions that describe how terms like region and channel relate to the business.
o.c: Add more columns from the underlying tables to give Genie access to a broader set of data points for reasoning.
o.d: Add descriptions to columns using Unity Catalog so Genie can use them as context during query generation.
o.e: Include example queries that reflect how business users refer to the data in everyday language.

e: Adding descriptions in Unity Catalog provides semantic context (D), and providing example queries helps Genie map business terminology to the correct SQL logic (E).

p: A data analyst filters rows where the `tags` array includes the value 'sql'... How should the analyst query to filter for rows where the `tags` array contains 'sql'?
e: To check for the existence of a value within an array column in Databricks SQL, the `array_contains()` function must be used.

p: A data analyst needs to programmatically mark the `sales_data` table in Unity Catalog as deprecated so that users across their organization can clearly see that it is no longer recommended for use. Which SQL command should they use?
e: The standard way to mark a table's certification status in Unity Catalog is by setting the system tag `system.certification_status`.

p: A data analyst is setting up a new AI/BI Genie space in Databricks to support natural language querying and ensure high-quality, governed responses. Which component is essential for configuring an effective Genie space that returns accurate and useful results?

o.a: Well-annotated datasets registered to Unity Catalog, curated sample queries, and domain-specific instructions
o.b: A standalone chatbot application integrated with Databricks through custom APIs for user interaction
o.c: A dedicated physical server allocated for the Genie space to maximize availability and scalability
o.d: An external data warehouse configured to store and replicate all data used by the Genie space

e: Genie relies heavily on the semantic layer: rich metadata (descriptions) in Unity Catalog, verified sample SQL queries, and clear instructions to generate accurate answers.

p: A data analyst wants to implement a use case that requires managing both structured and unstructured data. How will Unity Catalog help in this scenario?

o.a: It allows for the management of both structured data and unstructured data through objects such as tables and volumes.
o.b: It requires all unstructured data to be converted into Delta Lake format before it can be managed.
o.c: It manages structured data in tabular format and unstructured files like images in blob storage.
o.d: It can catalog data coming from relational databases, excluding files and non-tabular data.

e: Unity Catalog manages structured data via Tables and unstructured data (files, images) via Volumes, providing a unified governance layer.

p: A data analyst is reviewing the status of alerts in the Databricks SQL Alerts listing page. One alert was recently executed, and the monitored value met the defined condition and exceeded the threshold. Which status should appear for this alert in the listing?

o.a: Status: TRIGGERED
o.b: Status: YES
o.c: Status: SUCCESS
o.d: Status: OK

e: When an alert's condition is evaluated as true (threshold met), the status is reported as `TRIGGERED`.

p: A data analyst wants to generate insights from large, complex datasets. The analyst needs to quickly understand the meaning of various data columns, ask questions in natural language, and receive AI-driven recommendations for optimizing data queries and workflows. Which Databricks component is prima

o.a: Genie Spaces
o.b: Data Intelligence Engine
o.c: Unity Catalog
o.d: Databricks Assistant

e: The Data Intelligence Engine (formerly Databricks IQ) is the underlying AI engine that understands your data's semantics to power features like Genie and Assistant.

p: A data analyst needs to quickly estimate unique user sessions... What is the primary advantage of using APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT instead of COUNT_DISTINCT?

o.a: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT provides exact counts, while COUNT_DISTINCT only provides estimates
o.b: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT can only be used with string columns, while COUNT_DISTINCT works with numeric columns
o.c: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT uses the HyperLogLog++ algorithm to provide fast approximate counts with configurable accuracy
o.d: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT requires less memory by storing only the first 1000 unique values

e: It trades a small amount of accuracy for significant performance gains using the HyperLogLog++ algorithm, which is ideal for massive datasets.

p: A data analyst has noticed that a key dashboard is loading slowly and suspects a specific SQL query may be causing performance issues. To diagnose the root cause, the analyst wants to review query execution characteristics such as execution time, data scanned, and rows processed over time. How shoul

o.a: Use the SQL Dashboard Editor to identify slow-performing queries by reviewing visualization types and layout.
o.b: Use the Query Profiler to examine long-term trends in query performance across multiple executions.
o.c: Use Query Insights to view metrics such as duration, rows read, and execution history for the query.
o.d: Use Lakehouse Monitoring to view real-time alerts and trends across all data pipelines that run in Unity Catalog.

e: Query Insights (part of Query History/Performance view) allows users to analyze historical performance trends, execution counts, and resource usage for specific queries.

p: A data analyst needs to automate scheduled ETL jobs that ingest and transform data from multiple sources. The analyst wants to use multiple programming languages for flexibility and ensure that the pipeline can automatically handle schema changes as new data arrives. Which approach in Databricks sho

o.a: Separate Delta tables for each data source with fixed schemas
o.b: Unity Catalog with manual ETL scripts and cron-based scheduling
o.c: Databricks Workflows with Apache Spark notebooks and manual schema management
o.d: Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines with Auto Loader

e: Declarative Pipelines (like DLT) combined with Auto Loader provide schema evolution support and multi-language capabilities for robust ETL.

p: A data analyst is curating a Genie space for the marketing team. To ensure accurate and context-aware responses, the analyst includes curated Unity Catalog tables and sample questions. Which additional step can the analyst take to maximize trust and reuse of frequently asked queries?

o.a: Disable the use of domain instructions to prevent bias in AI-generated answers.
o.b: Enable automatic query generation so users receive instant responses without review.
o.c: Allow users to edit the underlying datasets to improve Genie responses.
o.d: Mark commonly used queries as Trusted Assets after verifying their correctness.

e: Marking verified queries as 'Trusted Assets' certifies them as accurate, encouraging users to rely on these pre-validated answers.

p: A data analyst is using Databricks Unity Catalog. The datasets are tagged by sensitivity, and confidential data is marked with the tag key `confidential`. The data analyst needs to quickly find all tables tagged as confidential in the Databricks workspace search bar. Which search key text should the

o.a: confidential:true
o.b: tag-confidential
o.c: tag:confidential
o.d: search tag = 'confidential'

e: The workspace search uses the syntax `tag:<tag_key>` to filter assets by a specific tag in Unity Catalog.

p: A data analyst is troubleshooting a query in Databricks SQL that fails when processing large datasets. Logs indicate the job aborts due to resource constraint errors. Which Query Profile metric should the analyst use to identify the operator causing resource overuse?

o.a: Shuffle read size per operator
o.b: Time spent per operator
o.c: Memory peak per operator
o.d: Bytes spilled to disk per operator

e: Memory peak per operator directly shows the maximum RAM consumed by a specific stage/operator, identifying the culprit for OOM (Out Of Memory) errors.

p: A data analyst needs to improve the performance of a daily sales report that aggregates data from a large transactions table. The report is run multiple times a day, but the underlying data only changes once daily. Which approach should the analyst use?

o.a: Create a materialized view that precomputes the daily sales aggregation.
o.b: Use a dynamic view to compute the aggregation on each query.
o.c: Use a standard view and schedule a notebook to cache results.
o.d: Set up a streaming table to ingest new sales data in real time.

e: Materialized views precompute and store the results. Since the source data changes only once a day, this avoids recomputing the heavy aggregation for every report run.

p: A data analyst is working interactively in a Databricks notebook. The analyst executes a SQL query using `%sql` and wants to turn the result into a line chart showing weekly user counts over time. Which step allows the analyst to create the chart directly in the notebook?

o.a: Save the query as a table, export it to Excel, and use Excel's charting tools.
o.b: Wrap the SQL query in a Python plotly express call using %python.
o.c: Use the display() function or %sql to run the query, then click the + icon in the result cell to add a visualization.
o.d: Use %sql to run the query, then copy the result into a new dashboard to access visualization options.

e: Databricks notebooks have a built-in visualization feature. Running a query with `%sql` (or `display()`) provides a '+' button in the results to instantly add charts.

p: Despite having `SELECT` permission on tables and `USAGE` on schemas, a data analyst is unable to access objects. Which action enables the data analyst to access the objects?

o.a: Grant MANAGE TABLE access.
o.b: Grant MANAGE DATABASE access on the containing catalog.
o.c: Grant USE CATALOG on the containing catalog.
o.d: Grant OWNERSHIP of the table to the Data Analyst.

e: In Unity Catalog's hierarchy, you must have `USE CATALOG` on the parent catalog (and `USE SCHEMA`) to access any object inside it, regardless of table-level permissions.

p: A data analyst team wants to understand the best practices and limitations of caching in Databricks. What is the limitation when using caching to reduce development time and query latency?

o.a: Query result caching works best with non-deterministic queries like NOW().
o.b: Caching CSV or JSON files with Delta Cache is fully supported.
o.c: Delta Cache (disk cache) automatically caches Parquet files on local SSDs ... but only supports Parquet files stored on Azure Blob Storage or Azure Data Lake.
o.d: Spark caching always improves performance and should be applied liberally.

e: The Delta Cache (Disk Cache) is optimized specifically for Parquet files (the format of Delta tables) and works with supported cloud object storage systems.

p: A data analyst is setting up an AI/BI Genie space. They notice that Genie is struggling to correctly join tables because the relationship between `orders.cust_id` and `customers.id` is not explicitly defined in the metadata. Which Unity Catalog feature should the analyst use to fix this and improve

o.a: Define a Primary Key on `customers.id` and a Foreign Key on `orders.cust_id`.
o.b: Create a materialized view that pre-joins the tables.
o.c: Write a 'System Instruction' telling Genie to always join these tables.
o.d: Use Liquid Clustering on both columns.

e: Even though PK/FK constraints are not enforced in Databricks, defining them provides critical metadata that Genie uses to automatically understand the data model and join tables correctly.

p: You are querying a shared table provided by a partner via Delta Sharing. You want to understand who pays for the compute costs when you execute a `SELECT` query against this shared table.

o.a: The data provider pays for compute; you pay for storage.
o.b: You (the data consumer) pay for the compute resources used to query the data.
o.c: Compute costs are split 50/50 between provider and consumer.
o.d: There are no compute costs for shared tables.

e: In the Delta Sharing model, storage and compute are decoupled. The provider pays for hosting the data (storage), but the consumer must bring their own compute (SQL Warehouse) to process and read it.

p: An analyst needs to ingest a large volume of JSON files from cloud storage into a Delta table using Databricks SQL. The schema of these JSON files evolves frequently (new columns are added). Which SQL function should be used to ingest these files while automatically handling schema evolution?

o.a: read_files() with the 'cloud_files' format
o.b: COPY INTO with default settings
o.c: INSERT INTO ... SELECT FROM json.`path`
o.d: CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE

e: In Databricks SQL, `read_files` invokes Auto Loader (format `cloud_files`), which is specifically designed to handle schema evolution and efficient incremental ingestion of files.

p: You have a table `events` that uses Liquid Clustering. Over time, you notice query performance degrading slightly as new data is added. What command should you schedule to run periodically to maintain optimal layout?

o.a: VACUUM events
o.b: ANALYZE TABLE events COMPUTE STATISTICS
o.c: OPTIMIZE events
o.d: REORG TABLE events APPLY (PURGE)

e: For Liquid Clustering, `OPTIMIZE` incrementally re-clusters the data based on the defined clustering keys to ensure data is co-located for fast skipping.

p: A data analyst creates a Materialized View (MV) to speed up a complex dashboard query. However, the refresh of the MV fails. Upon investigation, they realize they are using a Standard SQL Warehouse. Why did the refresh fail?

o.a: Materialized Views require a Serverless or Pro SQL Warehouse.
o.b: Materialized Views can only be refreshed by Admin users.
o.c: The underlying tables were not Delta tables.
o.d: Standard Warehouses cannot write data.

e: Materialized Views leverage advanced incremental computation features that are not available in the 'Standard' tier SQL Warehouses. You must use Pro or Serverless.

p: You are browsing the Databricks Marketplace to find a weather dataset to enrich your sales analysis. Once you 'install' a data product from the Marketplace, how does it appear in your workspace?

o.a: As a set of CSV files in DBFS.
o.b: As a read-only Catalog in Unity Catalog.
o.c: As a Dashboard.
o.d: You must download it via API first.

e: Marketplace installs create a new Catalog (or schema) in your Unity Catalog. These contain read-only tables that you can query immediately without copying data (Zero-Copy).

p: An analyst wants to filter a high-cardinality column `session_id` in a 5TB table. They originally used Hive-style partitioning on `session_id`, but this caused performance issues. They switched to Liquid Clustering. What was the specific performance issue caused by partitioning on a high-cardinality

o.a: Data Skew
o.b: Small Files Problem
o.c: Metadata locking
o.d: Predicate pushdown failure

e: Partitioning by a high-cardinality column (like unique IDs) creates thousands or millions of physical directories with tiny files. This overwhelms the metadata service and degrades performance.

p: You want to share a dashboard with a stakeholder who does NOT have a Databricks account. You want them to receive an updated PDF of the dashboard every Monday morning. Which feature allows this?

o.a: This is not possible; all users must have accounts.
o.b: Dashboard Subscription with 'Destinations' configured for external email.
o.c: Publish to Web.
o.d: Share via Delta Sharing.

e: In modern Databricks Dashboards, you can configure a Schedule with a Subscription Destination to send artifacts (PDFs) to email addresses outside the workspace, provided admin policies allow it.

p: When defining 'Trusted Assets' in an AI/BI Genie space, what is the primary benefit?

o.a: It encrypts the data.
o.b: It guides the AI to prioritize these specific tables when generating answers, reducing hallucinations.
o.c: It speeds up query performance by caching the assets.
o.d: It prevents users from querying any other table.

e: Trusted Assets act as a curated allow-list. It tells Genie: 'Use these tables to answer questions,' ensuring the AI doesn't pick up irrelevant or temporary tables from the catalog.

p: An analyst runs `DELETE FROM my_table WHERE id = 1`. They want to confirm that the data is physically removed from storage immediately to comply with a GDPR 'Right to be Forgotten' request. Is the DELETE command sufficient?

o.a: Yes, DELETE removes data physically.
o.b: No, they must run `VACUUM my_table RETAIN 0 HOURS` to remove physical files.
o.c: No, they must run `OPTIMIZE`.
o.d: No, they must drop the table.

e: `DELETE` in Delta Lake is a soft-delete (logical). The data remains in history for Time Travel. To strictly remove physical files immediately, `VACUUM` with 0 retention is required (ignoring the default safety retention check).

p: How do you define Liquid Clustering on a Delta table when creating it using SQL?

o.a: CREATE TABLE ... PARTITIONED BY (col1)
o.b: CREATE TABLE ... CLUSTER BY (col1, col2)
o.c: CREATE TABLE ... OPTIMIZE ZORDER BY (col1)
o.d: CREATE TABLE ... WITH CLUSTERING = TRUE

e: `CLUSTER BY` is the specific DDL syntax to enable Liquid Clustering. `PARTITIONED BY` is for Hive-style partitioning, and `ZORDER` is an optimization command, not a creation clause.

p: In Unity Catalog, you define a Primary Key and a Foreign Key relationship between two tables. You then attempt to insert an order with a `customer_id` that does not exist in the `customers` table. What happens?

o.a: The insert fails with a 'Constraint Violation' error.
o.b: The insert succeeds.
o.c: The insert is quarantined in a 'Bad Records' table.
o.d: The insert succeeds, but the `customer_id` is set to NULL.

e: In Databricks, Primary and Foreign Keys are 'Informational Constraints'. They are used for documentation and query optimization (and by Genie), but they are NOT enforced during data ingestion.

p: You are analyzing query performance using System Tables. You want to query the billing usage data programmatically. Which specific table should you query?

o.a: system.information_schema.columns
o.b: system.billing.usage
o.c: main.default.usage_logs
o.d: system.access.audit

e: `system.billing.usage` is the standard system table provided by Unity Catalog to expose consumption and pricing data for all workspaces.

p: In AI/BI Genie, what is the purpose of 'Draft Mode' vs 'Released Mode' (Publishing) for a space?

o.a: Draft Mode uses a smaller cluster to save costs.
o.b: Draft Mode is for the analyst to test and curate answers before end-users see them.
o.c: Released Mode makes the data public to the internet.
o.d: There is no difference; changes are always live.

e: Draft mode is the staging environment for the analyst to verify logic and 'System Instructions'. End-users only interact with the Released version to ensure quality.

p: A data analyst has added a query parameter named `date_param` to a SQL query powering a dashboard widget. However, when they change the value of the parameter widget at the top of the dashboard, the visualization does not update. What step did the analyst likely miss?

o.a: The analyst did not refresh the browser page.
o.b: The analyst needs to map the dashboard-level parameter to the widget-level parameter in the settings.
o.c: Parameters only work in the SQL Editor, not in Dashboards.
o.d: The dashboard subscription schedule has not been triggered yet.

e: Adding a parameter to a query doesn't automatically link it to the Dashboard's UI controls. You must explicitly map the Dashboard Parameter to the Query Parameter in the widget configuration.

p: An analyst needs to import a CSV file via `COPY INTO`, but the schema of the CSV might contain new columns in the future. They want these new columns to be automatically added to the target Delta table. Which option enables this?

o.a: ('mergeSchema' = 'true')
o.b: ('overwriteSchema' = 'true')
o.c: ('enforceSchema' = 'false')
o.d: ('autoEvolve' = 'true')

e: The `mergeSchema` option in `COPY INTO` (and Spark writes) allows the operation to evolve the target table's schema by adding any new columns found in the source data.

p: You want to restrict access to specific rows in the `employees` table so that analysts can only see employees from their own country. To which object do you apply the Row Filter function in Unity Catalog?

o.a: To the Dashboard.
o.b: To the SQL Warehouse.
o.c: To the Table definition.
o.d: To the User Group settings.

e: In Unity Catalog, security policies like Row Filters and Column Masks are attached directly to the Table definition. This ensures the security applies universally, regardless of how the table is accessed (SQL, Python, API).

p: An analyst needs to query a collection of PDF documents and images stored in cloud storage to perform analysis using AI functions. They want to manage access to these files using Unity Catalog governance. Which object should they create?

o.a: An External Table
o.b: A Volume
o.c: A Delta Live Table
o.d: A View

e: In Unity Catalog, **Volumes** are specifically designed to govern non-tabular data (unstructured data like PDFs, images, audio) while maintaining the benefits of centralized governance.

p: A team of data analysts wants to follow software engineering best practices for their SQL queries. They need to version control their queries, track changes over time, and collaborate using branches. Which Databricks feature enables this for SQL files?

o.a: Query History
o.b: Databricks Git Folders (Repos)
o.c: Workspace Browser
o.d: System Tables

e: Databricks SQL integrates with **Git Folders (formerly Repos)**. This allows analysts to save SQL files into a Git repository (GitHub, Azure DevOps, GitLab) to handle versioning, branching, and CI/CD.

p: A critical table was accidentally deleted yesterday. You need to find out exactly *who* ran the `DROP TABLE` command and *when*. Which system table should you query?

o.a: system.billing.usage
o.b: system.information_schema.tables
o.c: system.access.audit
o.d: system.storage.files

e: The `system.access.audit` table contains the audit logs for Unity Catalog. It records events like table creation, deletion (`DROP`), and access denials, including the user identity and timestamp.

p: You are calculating the average sales amount using `AVG(sales_amount)`. The column contains some `NULL` values. How does the `AVG` function handle these nulls in Databricks SQL?

o.a: It treats NULLs as 0 and includes them in the average calculation.
o.b: It ignores/skips the NULL values completely.
o.c: It returns NULL if any value in the column is NULL.
o.d: It throws a runtime error.

e: Standard SQL aggregate functions like `AVG`, `SUM`, `MIN`, and `MAX` automatically **ignore NULL values**. They do NOT treat them as zero. (e.g., Average of `[10, NULL, 20]` is `15`, not `10`).

p: In a Databricks Dashboard, you have a dataset with thousands of rows. You add a Bar Chart and a Table widget. You want to configure the dashboard so that when a user clicks on a specific bar in the chart, the Table widget automatically filters to show only the records related to that bar. What featu

o.a: Cross-filtering
o.b: Parameter Mapping
o.c: Z-Order Indexing
o.d: Dynamic Views

e: **Cross-filtering** allows interactions between widgets on a dashboard. Clicking a data point on one visualization applies a temporary filter to other visualizations based on the same dataset.

p: What access control model in Unity Catalog defines permissions based on tags or attributes assigned to data assets, users, and the environment rather than explicit role grants?

o.a: RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)
o.b: ACL (Access Control Lists)
o.c: ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control)
o.d: IAM (Identity and Access Management)
o.e: MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication)

e: ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) in Unity Catalog allows defining fine-grained policies based on attributes (tags) applied to data assets and users. It complements the existing privilege model, enabling row-level filtering and column masking through user-defined functions (UDFs) without explici

p: A data analyst needs to query data stored in an external PostgreSQL database directly from Databricks SQL without moving or copying the data. Which Databricks feature allows the analyst to create a federated catalog that points to the external database?

o.a: Delta Sharing
o.b: Lakehouse Federation
o.c: Auto Loader
o.d: COPY INTO
o.e: Databricks Connect

e: Lakehouse Federation allows creating federated catalogs in Unity Catalog that point to external databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, etc.), enabling direct queries from Databricks SQL without ETL or data movement.

p: A data analyst accidentally ran an UPDATE statement that corrupted data in a Delta table. They need to restore the table to its state as of version 5. Which command restores the table?

o.a: ROLLBACK TABLE my_table TO VERSION 5;
o.b: RESTORE TABLE my_table TO VERSION AS OF 5;
o.c: SELECT * FROM my_table VERSION AS OF 5;
o.d: UNDO TABLE my_table VERSION 5;
o.e: RESET TABLE my_table TO VERSION 5;

e: RESTORE TABLE my_table TO VERSION AS OF n restores the table to that specific version, undoing all subsequent changes. Note that SELECT * FROM table VERSION AS OF n only queries data at that version without actually restoring it.

p: In the context of data modeling for analytics, which of the following correctly describes a Star Schema?

o.a: A single flat table containing all columns and rows without any normalization
o.b: A central fact table surrounded by multiple denormalized dimension tables, optimized for analytical queries
o.c: A fully normalized schema with no data redundancy, used primarily for OLTP workloads
o.d: A schema with multiple fact tables and no dimension tables
o.e: A hierarchical schema where each level inherits the schema of the parent table

e: A Star Schema is an analytical modeling approach with a central fact table (containing measures like sales amount, quantity) connected to multiple denormalized dimension tables (like product, customer, time). It is optimized for fast reads and aggregations in reporting and dashboards.

p: A data analyst needs to ensure that when users query a table containing Social Security Numbers (SSNs), the SSN column displays only the last four digits (e.g., '***-**-1234') without modifying the actual stored data. Which Unity Catalog feature should the analyst use?

o.a: Row Filters
o.b: Data Tagging
o.c: Column Masking
o.d: Encryption at Rest
o.e: Access Control Lists

e: Column Masking in Unity Catalog uses User-Defined Functions (UDFs) to transform sensitive data at read time without modifying the underlying stored data. This allows different users to see masked or unmasked values based on their permissions and attributes.

p: A stakeholder has provided a data analyst with a single 20-row CSV file that needs to be quickly loaded into a Delta table for ad-hoc analysis. The analyst does not have access to cloud object storage. Which Databricks SQL feature allows the analyst to ingest this small file directly through the use

o.a: Auto Loader
o.b: COPY INTO
o.c: Upload File via the Databricks SQL UI
o.d: Delta Sharing
o.e: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT

e: The Upload File feature in the Databricks SQL UI is designed for lightweight ingestion of individual small files (CSV, JSON, etc.) without requiring object storage configuration. It is ideal for ad-hoc loading of small datasets like lookup tables or quick imports.

p: A data analyst is building a line chart in a Databricks SQL dashboard to visualize monthly revenue over two years. The analyst wants to overlay a visual indicator that helps identify anomalies and overall direction in the data. Which chart feature should the analyst enable?

o.a: Data Labels
o.b: Stacked Bars
o.c: Trend Lines
o.d: Pie Chart
o.e: Heat Map

e: Trend Lines overlay a regression line or moving average on top of data points, helping analysts visually spot anomalies, trends, and deviations from the expected pattern over time.

p: Which Unity Catalog feature automatically tracks the origin, transformations, and downstream consumers of a dataset at both the table and column level?

o.a: Data Masking
o.b: Data Lineage
o.c: Delta Time Travel
o.d: Liquid Clustering
o.e: Row Filters

e: Data Lineage in Unity Catalog automatically captures and visualizes the flow of data through tables, views, and queries. It shows column-level and table-level dependencies, making it easy to trace data origins, transformations, and downstream impacts.
